newsitem.title: USA: SBC lawsuit against intent of Congress--FCC.
newsitem.headline: SBC lawsuit against intent of Congress--FCC.

text.p: A lawsuit filed by SBC Communications Inc on Wednesday was an attempt to circumvent Congress' intent for telephone market competition, the Federal Communications Commission said.

"(Congress) sought to introduce much-needed competition in the local marketplace and, then, to allow new entrants in the long-distance market as well," FCC Commissioner Susan Ness said in a statement in response to the lawsuit.
"SBC's lawsuit appears to be an effort to circumvent that framework, to enable it to offer long-distance service without first opening its local markets to competition," she added.

Earlier on Wednesday, SBC filed in U.S. District Court in Wichita Falls, Texas, challenging sections of the Federal Telecommunications Act that restrict the regional Baby Bells from offering long-distance calling and other services.
SBC also said it would appeal last week's FCC ruling blocking the Baby Bell from offering long-distance service in Oklahoma.
